title: Truncating a fiber of a dependent sum: the truncation of the total space is unchanged
author: The Univalent Foundations Program

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.3.9 at source lines 629-634: for any family P : A -> type, trunc n (Sigma x:A, trunc n P(x)) is equivalent to trunc n (Sigma x:A, P(x)). The proof (source lines 636-649) is a complete quasi-inverse construction, not a citation: both directions have to be defined by induction on the n-truncation (source lines 645-646), which requires the induction principle to be applied to the family of n-types in question, and the two homotopies are then given by a second and third application of the same principle, with refl at the generators (source lines 647-648). Only after phi, psi, H and K are all in place does the equivalence follow. The statement records none of the four objects that have to be built.
